decade of double-digit growth or a sub-8% discount rate. Reverse DCF
demands ~10% revenue CAGR to 2035 — far above the company's own 7.5–8%

great business at a poor price: no new position; build a watchlist with
hard de-rating triggers.

in the ~55%-of-revenue Ratings segment). Not C (pure cyclical) because
~45% of revenue is recurring, subscription-style Analytics; not D
(Product-Platform Hybrid) because there is no hardware+installed-base
structure; not E (no material option value in the price — the market
price is the option).

EXPLICIT cycle normalization of the Ratings revenue line (issuance is
modeled as cyclical within a secular growth trend), plus:
  • Reverse DCF (expectations check)
  • Multiples vs history and peers
  • Market-implied SOTP cross-check (ratings vs analytics)

Step 0-3. Transition status: NONE. The mix (Ratings ~55% / Analytics
~45% of revenue) has been broadly stable for a decade [Estimate —
segment data not held in pack, SECTION 12]; management has publicly
committed to growing Analytics share, but the transition is gradual,
not an archetype shift. No blended engine required.

  (1) 12-yr revenue CAGR 7.9% and a 12-yr median operating margin of

  (2) ROIC >> WACC sustainably (GAAP ROE 62% FY2025 [Arithmetic]).
  (3) Recurring Analytics revenue gives earnings a floor that pure

  Error if Engine 2 (cycle-only) were used: it would ignore the
  compounding Analytics base and understate mid-cycle earnings.
  Error if Engine 4 (option) were used: it would treat a mature
  duopoly as a venture — analytically absurd.
